references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 27:15|Matthew 27:15] describes the same custom where the governor used to release a prisoner to the people at the feast. Matthew confirms the tradition that Luke refers to.
[ref:Mark 15:6|Mark 15:6] tells us that Pilate was accustomed to release one prisoner to them during the feast, which is the same custom mentioned in Luke 23:17.

In [ref:Joh 18:39|John 18:39], Pilate says directly to the Jews: "It is your custom that I release one person to you at Passover." This confirms the practice of releasing a prisoner during the Passover feast.
[ref:Luk 23:18-19|Luke 23:18-19] is the direct continuation where the crowd demands that Barabbas be released instead of Jesus, which is the result of the custom described in verse 17.
[ref:Matt 27:20-21|Matthew 27:20-21] shows how the chief priests and elders persuade the crowd to choose Barabbas – a direct parallel to the people's choice made possible by the custom in Luke 23:17.
